chunks: Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Al-Husayn ibn Saeed, from Fazalat ibn Ayoub, from Aban, from Ismail ibn Al-Fazl, who said:

I asked Abu Abdullah (peace be upon him) about the Qunut and what is to be said during it, so he (peace be upon him) said: 'Whatever Allah ordains upon your tongue, and I do not know of anything fixed for it.'
ai.seo_question: What should be recited during Qunut in prayer?
ai.summary: In this narration from al-Kafi, Imam al-Sadiq (peace be upon him) clarifies that the Qunut supplication lacks a rigidly prescribed text, emphasizing that whatever naturally arises from the supplicant's tongue is valid. This highlights the Shia jurisprudential principle of flexibility (tawassu') in voluntary supplications, distinguishing it from fixed Quranic recitations. The hadith underscores the personal and spontaneous nature of Qunut, allowing for diverse expressions of devotion rather than enforcing a single canonical formula.

en.hubeali: Muhammad Bin Yahya, from Ahmad Bin Muhammad, from Al Husayn Bin Saeed, from Fazalat Bin Ayoub, from Aban, from Ismail Bin Al Fazl who said,
‘I asked Abu Abdullahasws about the Qunut and what is to be said during it’. So heasws said: ‘Whatever Allahazwj Ordains upon your tongue, and Iasws do not know of anything fixed for it’.
en.sarwar: 8. Muhammad ibn Yahya has narrated from Ahmad ibn Muhammad from al-Husayn ibn Sa‘id from Fadalah ibn Ayyub from Aban ibn ’Isma‘il ibn al-Fadl who has said the following: “

I once asked abu ’Abd Allah, ‘Alayhi al-Salam, about Qunut (supplication after recitation in second Rak‘at) and what is said in it. He (the Imam) said, ‘Say whatever Allah makes to come out from your tongue. I do not know of anything definite for it.’”
